headline: Discordia Server for 'People Who Think They're the Main Character' Hits 100,000 Members
subheadline: Community struggles with fundamental problem: everyone wants to be the protagonist
summary: A support community for main character syndrome has grown massive—but governance has proven impossible.
content:
A Discordia server created for people who believe they're "the main character" has reached 100,000 members, becoming one of the platform's largest communities—and most ungovernable.

The server, titled "Protagonist Support Group," was founded in 2023 as a space for people to discuss their sense that they're the central figure in a narrative everyone else is supporting. It has since become a case study in what happens when 100,000 main characters occupy the same space.

"Every conversation becomes about them," explained founder @NarrativeCore, who has stepped back from active moderation. "Which... I guess is the point. But it makes it hard to have announcements. I tried to post server rules and 847 people responded explaining how the rules should center their specific journey."

The server's structure has evolved to accommodate its unique population. There are no moderators—only "deuteragonists" who support the main characters in maintaining order. Every member has their own channel, as shared channels resulted in "protagonist collision events" where users argued about whose story arc took precedence.

"I joined thinking I'd find my people," said member @ChroniclesOfMe. "But it turns out when everyone's the main character, you're just an NPC in their story. That's... actually been really humbling."

The server's most active channel is #am-i-the-main-character, where users post life events and others vote on whether it's sufficiently narratively significant. Most posts receive "side character energy" ratings, leading to existential spirals.

Psychologists have taken interest in the community as a study in narcissism and self-perception. Dr. Patricia Huang called it "the most efficient empathy-building exercise I've ever seen. Nothing cures main character syndrome like 99,999 other main characters."

At press time, the server was debating whether to elect a leader. All 100,000 members have nominated themselves.
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
